newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's NEC mulls Johnnic's future path.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's NEC mulls Johnnic's future path.

text.p: Black investment group the National Empowerment Consortium (NEC) is mulling the future path of the jewel in its crown, a controlling stake in conglomerate Johnnic -- and industry sources said Thursday it was considering a wide range of options.

NEC executives have just completed a three-day meeting in Cape Town to assess plans for Johnnic, which has a span of investments from a controlling stake in publishing empire Times Media Ltd to 13.9 percent of South African Breweries Ltd.
"They (NEC executives) have been looking at a long-term strategy. The results will come through in five to seven years," a source close to the talks said.
An official NEC statement said the talks had examined prospects for each of Johnnic's investments.
"The purpose of the session...was for the financial advisers and Johnnic management to update NEC on the latest developments within each of the underlying group of companies," the statement said.

There has been some market speculation that the NEC would want to sell its stake in SAB -- one of South Africa's top blue-chip firms -- in order to focus on firms where it could exercise more managerial control.

The cash raised from selling the investment would also help pay off the debts incurred when NEC bought its Johnnic stake from Anglo American Corp for about 2.7 billion rand in South Africa's biggest black empowerment.
Sources said the idea had been discussed at the meeting, but cast doubt on whether it would be recommended.
"There has been a lot of speculation about that. I am not sure that that would be a route they (NEC) would want to go down," the source said.
A wide range of other strategies had also been mooted, he added.
"It was one of those meetings where maybe 50 ideas are brought up and most will not be accepted and at the end of the day you will come out with just a couple...it is a long-term process."
There was also speculation that Johnnic's new non-executive chairman Cyril Ramaphosa had been nominated to be Times Media's new chairman.

Times Media chief operating officer Lawrence Clark said he was unaware of any such nomination for the non-executive post, but added it was likely that the firm's board would approve Ramaphosa were his name to be put forward.
"It is a matter for the NEC as to who they put forward...I would not see any problem (with Ramaphosa)," he told Reuters.

A spokeswoman for Ramaphosa -- a former mine union leader during the apartheid era -- said he had been considered for the Times Media job at the Cape Town meeting, but nothing had been firmly decided.
"There were suggestions made, but nothing has been finalised yet," she said.
